# Cairn System Rules Summary

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow by a fixed amount (the stride) plus a bonus. The bonus equals how many complete stride-lengths fit into the current height (integer division). So taller cairns grow more efficiently—each pulse sets up a stronger next pulse.

Formula: New Height = Old Height + Stride + (Old Height ÷ Stride)

## Multiple Pulses
You must apply pulses one at a time in sequence. You cannot skip steps because each pulse changes the height, which changes the bonus for the next pulse. The bonuses accelerate as the height increases.

## Leaks
After a pulse, some marks drain away proportional to the cairn's new height. The leak size (divisor) determines the drainage rate: smaller divisors mean more loss.

Formula: Marks Lost = New Height ÷ Leak Size (rounded down)
Final Height = New Height - Marks Lost

## Drain Cycles
A drain cycle combines one pulse followed by one leak. You repeat these cycles in sequence, with each cycle's starting height being the previous cycle's final height.

## Finding Origins (Working Backwards)
There's no reverse formula because integer division loses information. Instead, you test candidate starting heights by pulsing them forward until one matches the target final height.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine using weighted percentages from each. The shorter cairn provides a bonus (tether) divided by a tether divisor. Based on the patterns observed, the tether component doesn't appear to be added to the final result in the way initially described.
